summary: Cloud Guardian LLC is a North Brunswick, NJ managed service provider and MSSP selling managed IT, a 24/7 SOC/MDR stack (branded cGuard Security Suite), vCIO work, cabling/VoIP, and a newer ISO/IEC 42001 AI-governance and NJ Cyber JIF compliance practice. It publishes flat per-user pricing with no seat minimum, a free written assessment, and same-day onsite coverage across the Tri-State area plus remote support nationwide, and it already markets an AI support agent that auto-resolves common tickets. The site is a large programmatic SEO build (106 city pages, 10 industry pages) that reads as a lean, owner-operated shop rather than a staffed enterprise MSP.

facts.fact: Headquartered at 643 Georges Rd, North Brunswick Township, NJ 08902; the company is described as a New Jersey limited liability company in its own services agreement.

Service lines include managed IT/help desk, endpoints and cloud, email and cloud migrations, VoIP, structured cabling and wireless surveys, plus an eight-part 'cGuard Security Suite' spanning EDR, MDR/24/7 SOC, email security, identity and MFA, dark web monitoring, backup and recovery, firewall/network and security awareness.

Publishes list pricing: Pay As You Go $25/$50 per user per month (Core/Pro), Managed User $100/$150, Power User $200/$225; $150/hour for all out-of-scope work billed in 15-minute increments; no minimum seat count and no three-year term.

Markets a free assessment that inventories devices, accounts, licensing and breach exposure, with a written findings report the prospect keeps whether or not they hire the firm; claims most issues are resolved in about seven minutes and that callers reach a live person rather than a callback.

Support is routed through a launchpad of channels — phone or text on (732) 743-5472, a ticket form, a one-time-link remote session, an AI Support Agent, and a client portal that the page says is 'being rolled out to managed clients now.'

The services agreement states AI is used in endpoint detection, email security, monitoring, log correlation, alert triage, ticket summarization and routing, documentation and scripting, with some protective actions (quarantine, endpoint isolation, session disable) taken automatically without a human in the loop.

Contract terms include 18% annual interest plus a $50-per-week administrative charge on overdue invoices, ten-day suspension notice for non-payment, and 180 days' written notice to exit where no fixed term is stated.

Onsite service is routine within roughly 50 miles of the North Brunswick office with same- or next-business-day response, remote support is sold nationwide, and onsite project work outside the region is handled by dispatched field technicians.
The site claims 30 years of combined team experience, 24/7/365 security operations, 10 industries with dedicated playbooks and 50 states covered remotely.

Runs a dedicated NJ Cyber JIF readiness practice for municipal and public entities, mapping the fund's ten published cyber controls to remediation and an annual attestation evidence pack, with pages per county JIF.
The service-areas section covers 106 city pages across NJ, NY, PA and CT; the sitemap shows every page last modified on 2026-10-26, consistent with a bulk programmatic build.
The blog holds six posts on generic MSP/AI topics (AI in IT consulting, AI risks, vCIO, NJ cyber JIF, IT for small business) with no named author bylines on the article page checked.

operations_signals: Intake runs through a quoted-pricing form (business name, user counts, email platform, existing services) plus a free-assessment booking and a 'next steps' discovery-meeting funnel; nothing is self-serve checkout, every path ends in a human quote (https://cloud-guardian.com/pricing/).
Pricing page promises a same-business-day written quote and says a person, not a bot, reads each submission, which points to manual quoting and scoping (https://cloud-guardian.com/pricing/).
Support intake is multi-channel: phone or text on one number, ticket form, remote screen-share session, and an AI Support Agent page for automated fixes (https://cloud-guardian.com/support/).
After-hours coverage is advertised 24/7/365 with a live engineer answering emergency calls; the contact page lists 24/7 support outside standard business hours (https://cloud-guardian.com/contact/).

Onsite dispatch is the constraint-heavy part of delivery: two-hour onsite minimum, next-business-day critical response inside 50 miles, and travel beyond 50 miles billable (https://cloud-guardian.com/agreement/).

Billing is per-user monthly with 15-minute time tracking and itemized invoices, and the agreement adds manual-feeling collections levers (18% interest, $50/week admin fee, ten-day suspension notice) (https://cloud-guardian.com/agreement/).
Client portal for ticket history, asset inventory and documentation is explicitly still rolling out, so much of that record-keeping is likely manual today (https://cloud-guardian.com/support/).
hiring_signals: No careers page exists: /careers/ returns HTTP 404 and the sitemap lists no jobs or team page, so hiring is not advertised on the site (https://cloud-guardian.com/sitemap.xml).

No open postings or company profile could be retrieved from Indeed, LinkedIn, ZipRecruiter, Glassdoor or a careers page during this research; job-board pages returned 403 to automated access and the web-search index was unavailable for this run (https://www.indeed.com/cmp/Cloud-Guardian-LLC).

Absence of a tiered help desk is stated as a selling point ('a ticket passes through two people who cannot fix it'), implying few or no L1 triage staff and heavy reliance on automation instead (https://cloud-guardian.com/pricing/).
review_themes: Only self-published testimonials were available: three short quotes on the managed IT page attributed to first names (Jessica, David, Alex) praising responsiveness and availability; not verifiable third-party reviews (https://cloud-guardian.com/services/itservices/).

Own marketing repeatedly claims fast human response — live answer in the queue, most issues fixed in about seven minutes — which is the claim most exposed if response capacity slips (https://cloud-guardian.com/pricing/).
No Google, Yelp, BBB or Trustpilot review content could be retrieved (403/JS-rendered pages), so real customer sentiment is unverified (https://www.yelp.com/biz/cloud-guardian-north-brunswick).
tech_footprint: Support portal lives on a subdomain (support.cloud-guardian.com) and is described as a portal for ticket history, asset inventory and documentation, rolled out to managed clients incrementally (https://cloud-guardian.com/support/).

Branded 'Guardian Console' with a live ticket/AI-triage demo on the homepage, and a marketed AI Support Agent that diagnoses and applies approved fixes in chat with an audit log (https://cloud-guardian.com/services/out-of-band/).

Publicly documented AI stack use: alert triage and enrichment, ticket summarization and routing, documentation drafting, automated quarantine/isolation actions, ISO/IEC 42001-aligned governance, and an AI subprocessor list available on request (https://cloud-guardian.com/agreement/).

Marketing site is a static build with hand-rolled CSS; the markup carries a Leadsy.ai visitor-identification tag and privacy-conscious analytics, per the privacy policy's IP-to-company matching disclosure (https://cloud-guardian.com/privacy/).
Inbound inquiries may be processed by third-party AI to draft replies, summarize and route them, per section 3 of the privacy policy (https://cloud-guardian.com/privacy/).

Structured data on the site declares a ProfessionalService with a Google Maps listing (CID) and a 24/7 opening-hours spec, plus Machine 365/Google Workspace, ISO/IEC 42001 and law-firm IT as known topics (https://cloud-guardian.com/blog/balancing-the-benefits-and-risks-of-ai-implementation/).
Publishes substantive content: a versioned client services agreement (v4.0, effective August 5, 2026) and privacy policy, plus a small blog with six articles (https://cloud-guardian.com/agreement/).
growth_signals: Expanded beyond classic MSP work into ISO/IEC 42001 AI management system certification support and an AI Support Agent product line, both new-service launches rather than core IT support (https://cloud-guardian.com/services/out-of-band/).

Built a public-sector vertical aimed at NJ municipal joint insurance funds (Cyber JIF), with county-level landing pages and three engagement tiers, suggesting a push into government accounts (https://cloud-guardian.com/services/cyber-jif/).

Large SEO footprint build-out: 106 city service-area pages across four states plus per-industry pages, all stamped with one last-modified date, indicating a recent marketing expansion (https://cloud-guardian.com/sitemap.xml).

Pricing model is deliberately volume-scalable (no seat minimum, per-user flat fee, 15-minute billing), positioned to undercut legacy MSPs on labor cost through automation (https://cloud-guardian.com/pricing/).

Service area extends to Manhattan, Brooklyn, Philadelphia and remote support in all 50 states, i.e. growth is geographic and remote rather than new branch offices (https://cloud-guardian.com/service-areas/).
decision_maker: Unknown — no owner, founder, GM or leadership name appears on the about, contact, agreement, privacy or blog pages, and no company page could be retrieved (LinkedIn returned 403).

inferences.inference: Cloud Guardian is likely a very small team (owner plus a handful of engineers), not a staffed 24/7 SOC of its own.
inferences.reasoning: It advertises '30 yrs combined experience' rather than headcount, has no careers or team page, sells on having no tiered help desk, and promises 'a named engineer' per account — all patterns of a lean shop leaning on vendor tooling and automation for round-the-clock coverage.

inferences.inference: Their 24/7 SOC and after-hours promise is probably delivered through vendor MDR platforms plus on-call staff rather than an in-house night shift.
inferences.reasoning: The services agreement lists automated protective actions (isolating endpoints, disabling sessions) as the night-time control and describes MDR as a feature of licensed vendor platforms, which is how small MSSPs cover 24/7 without staffing it.

inferences.inference: Inbound sales and quoting are still human-bottlenecked despite the AI positioning.
inferences.reasoning: Every path (pricing form, free assessment, discovery meeting) terminates in a person reading the submission and returning a written quote the same day; there is no instant quoting or self-serve checkout.

inferences.inference: Compliance evidence collection for NJ Cyber JIF clients is the most repetitive, agent-friendly workload they carry.
inferences.reasoning: Their own page describes assembling one document per control per entity, refreshing evidence before every annual attestation, and repeating the cycle for each borough or authority — high-volume, template-driven document work.

inferences.inference: They are as much a competitor as a prospect for an AI agent consultancy.
inferences.reasoning: They already sell an 'AI Support Agent' and ISO/IEC 42001 AI governance services, so any engagement would likely be subcontracting delivery capacity or productizing their internal tooling rather than teaching them AI basics.

inferences.inference: The 106 city pages are programmatic SEO and likely thin on unique local proof, which caps their lead quality.
inferences.reasoning: All pages share one last-modified date, follow a county-plus-industry template, and the site shows no case studies or named client references to substantiate local claims.

data_gaps: No employee count, revenue, founding year or NJ business-registry record could be verified; Bizapedia and OpenCorporates pages were JavaScript-only and no search index was reachable.

Hiring data missing: no careers page (404), and Indeed, LinkedIn, Glassdoor, ZipRecruiter and Trustpilot all returned 403 or JS-only pages; web_search returned provider errors (Exa rate limit, OpenAI quota) for every query, so no job-posting history could be reviewed.
Customer reviews missing: Google Business Profile (CID 5493292995205407246), Yelp and BBB pages could not be rendered, so no third-party review themes, ratings or complaint patterns were retrievable.
No decision-maker name published anywhere on the site; no leadership or team page exists in the sitemap.
No news coverage, awards, press mentions or client case studies were found on the site or accessible externally.
Blog authorship and publication dates are not shown on article pages, so content cadence could not be measured.
